advances: The proposed one-dimensional variational inequality (9) is false, even for constant interval-section families realized by rational rectangles and satisfying the full two-parameter midpoint inclusion, both crossing equalities, and all three inequalities \(c_i+m\ge\theta\). The registered support-contact conclusion is not refuted by this example: it holds with equality. What fails is the stronger replacement of the actual \(Q_{23}+R_{23}\) overlap by the gap-versus-overlap lower bound.
author: mp_r66_empty_full_gap_overlap_variation
proof:
First,
\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1,\qquad
L_1+L_2+L_3=-\frac{3181}{150}<-1.
\]
The three gradients are nonzero and pairwise nonparallel. Also
\(L_1=\min_{A_0}f_1=0\).

Because \(L_1=0\) and \(L_2=L_3\), each of the three local coordinate
maps
\[
(p_1,p_2-p_3),\qquad(q_1,q_2-q_3),\qquad(r_1,r_2-r_3)
\]
is simply \((x,y)\). Hence its area Jacobian is \(1\), and the section
families are
\[
I_s=\left[-\frac{15}{2},\frac{15}{2}\right]
\quad\left(0\le s\le\frac{953}{75}\right),
\]
\[
J_t=\left[-\frac12,\frac12\right]
\quad\left(-\frac1{10}\le t\le\frac9{10}\right),
\]
\[
H_z=[-4,4]
\quad\left(-\frac{729}{80}\le z\le8\right),
\]
and are empty outside the displayed projection intervals. Their lower
endpoints are convex and their upper endpoints are concave.

The exact Minkowski average is
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}
=
\left[-\frac1{20},\frac{2041}{300}\right]\times[-4,4]
\subseteq K.
\]
Therefore, for every admissible pair \((s,t)\),
\[
\frac{I_s+J_t}{2}=[-4,4]=H_{(s+t)/2},
\]
so the full two-parameter midpoint inclusion holds. If desired, these
three rectangles are the integer slices of the rational polytope
\[
\operatorname{conv}\bigl(
(\{0\}\times A_0)\cup(\{1\}\times K)\cup(\{2\}\times A_2)
\bigr);
\]
the inclusion above shows that its slice at the middle integer is
exactly \(K\).

The areas are
\[
M=\frac{953}{5},\qquad
m=1,\qquad
k=\frac{1369}{10},
\]
and consequently
\[
\theta=\frac{2(M+m+k)}9=73.
\]
On \(A_0\),
\[
p_2\le0\iff y\le x-\delta,\qquad
p_3\le0\iff y\ge\delta-x.
\]
Since
\[
\delta=\frac{953}{75}+\frac{15}{2},
\]
each of these two halfplanes meets \(A_0\) only along a null corner.
Thus
\[
u_1=u_2=u_3=0.
\]

On \(A_2\),
\[
q_1=x,\qquad
q_2\le0\iff y\le2+\delta+x,\qquad
q_3\le0\iff y\ge-2-\delta-x.
\]
Both latter inequalities hold throughout \(A_2\). Therefore
\[
v_1=\frac1{10},\qquad v_2=v_3=1.
\]

On \(K\), \(c_1\) is immediate:
\[
c_1=8\cdot\frac{729}{80}=\frac{729}{10}.
\]
For \(c_2\), the cutting inequality is \(y\le1+x\). Its section length
is zero for \(x\le-5\), is \(x+5\) for \(-5\le x\le3\), and is \(8\)
for \(3\le x\le8\). Hence
\[
c_2=\int_{-5}^{3}(x+5)\,dx+\int_3^8 8\,dx
=32+40=72.
\]
Reflection in \(y=0\) gives \(c_3=72\). Thus both crossing equalities
hold:
\[
c_i+u_i+v_i=72+0+1=73=\theta
\qquad(i=2,3).
\]
The three lower bounds also hold:
\[
c_1+m=\frac{739}{10}\ge73,\qquad
c_2+m=c_3+m=73.
\]
The contact cap of \(A_2\) is proper, since \(v_1=1/10<m\), and the
registered support-contact conclusion itself is an equality:
\[
c_1+v_1=\frac{729}{10}+\frac1{10}=73=\theta.
\]

It remains to evaluate the two sides of (9). On the contact side
\(x\le0\) of \(A_2\), both crossing-cap inequalities hold everywhere,
so
\[
\eta_2=2\left|A_2\cap\{x\le0\}\right|=\frac15.
\]
On the contact side \(x\le0\) of \(K\), each of the two symmetric
crossing caps has area
\[
\int_{-5}^{0}(x+5)\,dx=\frac{25}{2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\eta_K=25.
\]

The positive-\(q_1\) body is
\[
B=[0,9/10]\times[-1/2,1/2]
\]
up to null boundary sets. For every \(0<t\le9/10\),
\[
J_t\cap(-\infty,-2-\delta-t)=\varnothing,\qquad
J_t\cap(2+\delta+t,\infty)=\varnothing.
\]
Consequently \(T_2=T_3=\varnothing\),
\(\Gamma=(0,9/10]\), and
\(\Sigma_2=\Sigma_3=\varnothing\). It follows that
\[
\int_\Gamma |J_t|\,dt=\frac9{10},
\qquad
\int_{\Sigma_2\cap\Sigma_3}2(1+z)\,dz=0.
\]
Using \(u_2=u_3=0\), the left side of (9) is therefore
\[
0+\frac15+25+\frac9{10}=\frac{261}{10}.
\]
The right side is
\[
\frac{2M-m-k}{3}
=\frac{2(953/5)-1-1369/10}{3}
=\frac{811}{10}.
\]
Thus (9) fails by exactly \(55\).

The lost quantity can also be seen directly. Here \(Q_{23}=B\), so
\(|Q_{23}|=9/10\). In \(D=K\cap\{x>0\}\), the \(R_{23}\)-section has
length \(2(1+x)\) for \(0<x<3\) and length \(8\) for \(3\le x\le8\).
Hence
\[
|R_{23}|=\int_0^3 2(1+x)\,dx+\int_3^8 8\,dx=15+40=55.
\]
The bridge term records \(9/10\) but none of this \(55\), exactly
accounting for the failure.
statement:
In planar coordinates \((x,y)\), define
\[
f_1=x,\qquad
f_2=\frac{-1-x+y}{2},\qquad
f_3=\frac{-1-x-y}{2},
\]
\[
L_1=0,\qquad L_2=L_3=-\frac{3181}{300},
\qquad
\delta=-1-(L_1+L_2+L_3)=\frac{3031}{150},
\]
and the rational rectangles
\[
A_0=\left[0,\frac{953}{75}\right]\times
\left[-\frac{15}{2},\frac{15}{2}\right],
\]
\[
A_2=\left[-\frac1{10},\frac9{10}\right]\times
\left[-\frac12,\frac12\right],
\qquad
K=\left[-\frac{729}{80},8\right]\times[-4,4].
\]
Put
\[
M=|A_0|,\qquad m=|A_2|,\qquad k=|K|,
\qquad
\theta=\frac{2(M+m+k)}9.
\]
For \(i=1,2,3\), put
\[
u_i=|A_0\cap\{f_i\le L_i\}|,\qquad
v_i=|A_2\cap\{f_i\le-L_i\}|,\qquad
c_i=|K\cap\{f_i\le0\}|.
\]
Use the section coordinates and the quantities
\(I_s,J_t,H_z,P_\pm,T_2,T_3,\Gamma,\Sigma_2,\Sigma_3,
\eta_2,\eta_K\) occurring in (9). Then the section-coordinate
Jacobian is \(\kappa=1\), the full two-parameter inclusion
\[
\frac{I_s+J_t}{2}\subseteq H_{(s+t)/2}
\]
holds whenever both source sections are nonempty, and all the displayed
support-contact hypotheses hold. Nevertheless,
\[
u_2+u_3+\eta_2+\eta_K+
\kappa\left(
\int_\Gamma |J_t|\,dt+
\int_{\Sigma_2\cap\Sigma_3}2(1+z)\,dz
\right)
=\frac{261}{10}
<\frac{811}{10}
=\frac{2M-m-k}{3}.
\]
